design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized controlled trial where patients were randomly assigned to Crosseal or standard topical hemostatic agents using sealed envelopes with randomly permuted blocks stratified by surgeon.

domain_judgments.rationale: The random sequence was generated using randomly permuted blocks with variable block sizes by an independent statistician, allocation concealment was achieved with a sealed envelope system opened just prior to treatment, and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment allocation employed a sealed envelope system... Randomization envelopes were not opened until immediately prior to treatment, when the surgeon had determined that all discrete bleeding points had been controlled and that use of a topical hemostatic agent was necessary. Randomization was by patient, stratified by surgeon within each clinical center, using the method of randomly permuted blocks. A variable and undisclosed block size was used to reduce selection bias. A statistician who was not otherwise involved in the conduct of the study prepared the randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were blinded under anesthesia, no substantial unintended deviations occurred that could confound the effect of assignment, and an intention-to-treat analysis was performed for the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was single-blind, as the nature of the compared treatments made it impossible for the surgeon to be blinded. Insofar as possible, all staff, including data analysts, were blinded to treatment allocation... Analyses were done using both the efficacy-evaluable and all-patients-randomized (ie, intention-to-treat [ITT]) populations.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary outcome (time to hemostasis) were available for all 121 randomized patients in the ITT analysis, with very low attrition (5 patients total excluded from the per-protocol analysis).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All-patients-randomized analyses were based on 121 patients. Efficacy-evaluable analyses were based on 55 Crosseal (American Red Cross, Washington, DC) patients and 61 standard-treatment patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (time to hemostasis) is subjective and was evaluated directly by operating surgeons who were unblinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was single-blind, as the nature of the compared treatments made it impossible for the surgeon to be blinded... When the surgeon believed hemostasis was achieved, the liver surface was observed for 1 minute to confirm hemostasis... For control products applied with patches or gauze, the evaluation was made by the surgeon’s carefully lifting a corner of the product to check for bleeding.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was conducted under FDA monitoring with a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and reported both ITT and evaluable population analyses for the predefined primary and secondary outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The terms included in the model, prespecified in the statistical analysis plan, were treatment, surgeon, surgeon x treatment interaction, preoperative platelet count, type of liver resection, and whether argon beam coagulation was used. Analyses were done using both the efficacy-evaluable and all-patients-randomized (ie, intention-to-treat [ITT]) populations.

overall_summary: While the trial had robust randomization, allocation concealment, and complete follow-up, there are some concerns regarding risk of bias in outcome measurement because the primary endpoint (time to hemostasis) is subjective and was assessed by unblinded surgeons.

design_rationale: The study states that 62 patients were randomly allocated to receive either CL or FG using a sealed envelope procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a sealed envelope procedure was used, the method of sequence generation is not described, and it is unclear whether envelopes were sequentially numbered and opaque.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Then, through sealed envelope procedure, patients were allocated to the CL (AVITENE ®, Alcon Inc., Humacao, Puerto Rico) or FG (BERIPLAST ~ P, Beringwerke AB, Marburg, GermanY) : group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions were delivered surgically as intended per protocol during elective liver resection, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: If bleeding from the cut surface continued, further management for hemostasis was decided by the surgeons (N.N., H.K., Y.C.) ad libitum.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear to be fully available for all 62 randomized participants (31 per group) with no reported dropouts or losses to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinical characteristics of patients for the CL (n = 31) and FG (n = 31) groups is shown in Table 1.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary intraoperative outcome (achieving a completely dry cut surface) was subjective and assessed by the unblinded operating surgeons who knew the allocated intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In both the CL and the FG groups, the agents were judged to be effective in terms of hemostasis during surgery if the cut surface of liver appeared to be completely dry.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no indication of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, raising some concerns for selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The two groups were compared in regard to hemostatic efficacy during surgery, postoperative rebleeding, bile leakage, and other complications.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient details regarding sequence generation and envelope concealment, subjective intraoperative outcome evaluation by unblinded surgeons, and the lack of a pre-registered trial protocol.

design_rationale: The authors describe a prospective, multicentre, randomized clinical trial where patients were allocated to study arms using a pre-generated randomization scheme with sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: While sealed envelopes were used, there was an initial error discovered in the randomization schedule requiring mid-study regeneration of codes, and envelopes were not specifically described as sequentially numbered, opaque, or sealed in a tamper-evident manner, resulting in an unequal allocation (32 vs 18).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A 1 : 1 treatment randomization scheme, stratified by study centre and the presence of cirrhosis, was generated prior to the initiation of the study. Sealed envelopes were prepared for each stratum and each study centre and were opened in a sequential manner... After 14 patients had been randomized, it was discovered that the randomization was not a true permuted block randomization. Consequently, a new randomization code was produced and used to randomize subsequent patients (n = 36).

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were blinded (under general anesthesia during surgery), deviations were minimal (one patient received argon beam instead of control), and the primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: With the exception of one patient, all patients received the treatment to which they had been randomized. In one patient, haemostasis was achieved using an argon beam rather than with the control treatment as the investigator felt it was in the best interests of the patient to do so... All effectiveness analyses were performed using the intent-to-treat population, which included all randomized patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary intraoperative outcome data (time to haemostasis) were available and evaluated for all 50 randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All effectiveness analyses were performed using the intent-to-treat population, which included all randomized patients. The Kaplan–Meier method was used to estimate the distribution of time to haemostasis and to obtain the estimated median time to haemostasis for each treatment. Patients who did not achieve haemostasis within 10 min were censored at that time.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (operating surgeons) were unblinded, the visual determination of cessation of diffuse bleeding is subjective, and the measurement schedule was fundamentally asymmetric between groups (first assessment at 30 seconds vs. 3 minutes).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Upon application of the study treatment to the target bleeding site, a stopwatch was started. In the control group, according to the manufacturer’s instructions, the product was left in situ for 3 min, at which point the first inspection was made; this was followed by inspections every 30 s until bleeding stopped. In the Veriset™ haemostatic patch group, the bleeding site was inspected every 30 s from application of the patch until bleeding stopped.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registry identifier or pre-published analysis protocol is cited, and several post hoc analyses were required to account for the differential observation windows and baseline imbalances.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although the study was a non-inferiority study, the sample size was determined for a one-sided test for superiority based on the primary effectiveness endpoint (median time to haemostasis) with a power of 80%, an alpha of 0.025... Post hoc effectiveness analyses were conducted to address the imbalance between groups at baseline in bleeding severity and area, and the difference and discrepancy in the first observation period following application of the device

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to Domain 4 (measurement of the outcome), as unblinded surgeons assessed the subjective primary endpoint of time to haemostasis using fundamentally different inspection schedules between the experimental and control arms (30 seconds vs. 3 minutes). There were also some concerns regarding the randomization process and potential selective reporting.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial in which eligible patients were randomized 2:1, stratified by surgical indication and blocked within site.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study used stratified blocked randomization intraoperatively after identifying an eligible bleeding site, baseline characteristics were well-balanced, and there is no evidence of allocation compromise.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the procedure, eligible patients with an appropriate target bleeding site were randomized 2:1 to treatment with Fibrocaps plus gelatin sponge or gelatin sponge alone... Randomization was stratified by the 4 surgical indications and blocked within site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients received the assigned surgical intervention under general anesthesia in an intraoperative setting, and analyses included essentially all randomized and treated participants with no post-randomization deviations that could bias outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy and safety analyses included all treated patients... Two ineligible patients were not treated.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary efficacy outcome data (time to hemostasis within 5 minutes intraoperatively) were available for all 719 treated participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy and safety analyses included all treated patients. Efficacy analyses were conducted separately for each surgical indication. Time to hemostasis was summarized by Kaplan-Meier estimates of the TTH curves.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (the surgeons) were unblinded to treatment assignment, and assessing whether blood was seeping through or around the sponge every 30 seconds involves subjective judgment that could be influenced by knowledge of the intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary limitation of this study is the single-blind study design, which enabled the treating surgeons to be aware of the assigned treatments. Given the treatments evaluated, it was not possible to blind the investigator or surgeons involved in the care of the patient.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with clearly predefined endpoints and analysis procedures, and outcomes were reported comprehensively according to the plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT01527357) and EudraCT (2011-006174-47), and the predefined primary and secondary efficacy endpoints were reported according to a specified statistical plan.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias judgment is 'some concerns', driven by the lack of blinding of the surgeons who performed the subjective intraoperative outcome assessment (time to hemostasis). All other domains were judged as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial where adult and pediatric patients were intraoperatively randomized (1:1) to FSP or ORCG using a centralized interactive voice or web response system with randomly permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was centralized using interactive voice or web response system with randomly permuted blocks, ensuring allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A centralized interactive voice or web response system was used for intraoperative randomization (using the method of randomly permuted blocks) to conceal allocation until assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label due to product differences, treatment was administered intraoperatively according to a standard protocol, there were no reported non-protocol deviations affecting outcome, and an intention-to-treat (full analysis set) approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy analyses in adults were based on the full analysis set, which included all randomized adult patients with patients analyzed according to the treatment assigned at randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 224 randomized adult patients were included in the primary efficacy analysis, with no missing outcome data for intraoperative hemostasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 321 adult patients screened, 224 patients had minor to moderate bleeding from the hepatic resection area after primary hemostatic treatment and were intraoperatively randomized to FSP (n 114) or ORCG (n 110)... Efficacy analyses in adults were based on the full analysis set, which included all randomized adult patients with patients analyzed according to the treatment assigned at randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was unblinded and the outcome (intraoperative assessment of visible bleeding at 3 minutes) is subjective and evaluated directly by unblinded surgeons who knew the assigned treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blinding was not possible due to the difference in appearance of the 2 products... The primary end point was the proportion of adult patients with intraoperative hemostasis (no visible bleeding) at the target area within 3 minutes of application of the first treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01192022) with clearly specified primary and secondary outcomes and a pre-defined statistical analysis plan adhered to in the report.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a randomized, open-label study (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT01192022)... The primary end point was the proportion of adult patients with intraoperative hemostasis (no visible bleeding) at the target area within 3 minutes of application of the first treatment.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with robust randomization and complete data, but overall risk of bias is rated as 'some concerns' due to the open-label design where outcome assessors (surgeons) were unblinded while subjectively evaluating the primary endpoint of intraoperative hemostasis.

design_rationale: The study is described as two randomized controlled phase II trials where eligible patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to Fibrocaps plus gelatin sponge or gelatin sponge alone.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states that patients were randomized 2:1, but provides no details on sequence generation or allocation concealment methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: patients with mild or moderate bleeding during an open surgical procedure that necessitated the use of an adjunct to hemostasis were randomized within each study in a 2:1 ratio to treatment with Fibrocaps plus gelatin sponge (“Fibrocaps arm”) or gelatin sponge alone (“sponge-alone arm”).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trials were single-blind (patients blinded under anesthesia), surgery followed intended experimental protocols, deviations were minimal, and efficacy analyses adhered to the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Safety and efficacy of Fibrocaps applied directly or by spray device, in combination with gelatin sponge, was compared with that of gelatin sponge-alone in two randomized, single-blind controlled trials... Efficacy analyses were performed on an intent-to-treat basis, and safety analyses included all treated patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data (intraoperative time to hemostasis) were collected during surgery and available for all randomized participants in the intent-to-treat analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Assessment of hemostasis was made by carefully checking for bleeding through or around the gelatin sponge, starting at 1 min after application of study treatment and recurring every 1 min until hemostasis had been achieved or 10 min had elapsed, whichever came first... One additional patient was randomized but did not receive study treatment. Data for this patient are not included in this table or in the safety analyses but are included in the efficacy analyses (hepatic resection, intent-to-treat analysis set)

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome assessment of hemostasis was subjective and performed intraoperatively by unblinded surgeons who were aware of the intervention received.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Safety and efficacy of Fibrocaps applied directly or by spray device, in combination with gelatin sponge, was compared with that of gelatin sponge-alone in two randomized, single-blind controlled trials... Assessment of hemostasis was made by carefully checking for bleeding through or around the gelatin sponge, starting at 1 min after application of study treatment and recurring every 1 min until hemostasis had been achieved or 10 min had elapsed, whichever came first.

domain_judgments.rationale: The studies were prospectively registered with predefined primary and secondary endpoints (time to hemostasis and hemostasis at specified time intervals), which were reported as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: FC-002 US (clinicaltrials.gov: [NCT01256164]) was conducted at eight sites in the United States from FebruaryeOctober 2011. FC-002 NL (clinicaltrials.gov: [NCT01256190]; EudraCT number: 2010-020202-16) was conducted at five clinical sites in the Netherlands from December 2010 October 2011.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to Domain 4 (measurement of the outcome), as time to hemostasis was assessed intraoperatively by surgeons who were unblinded to treatment allocation. There are also some concerns regarding the randomization process due to lack of reported details on allocation sequence generation and concealment.

design_rationale: The study is described as an international, multicenter, randomized controlled trial where patients were allocated to treatment groups via a centralized telephone randomization system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized telephone randomization was used to conceal allocation sequence, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subsequently, randomization to either TachoSil or ABC was performed by calling a centralized telephone randomization system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The surgical trial delivered the interventions intraoperatively under protocol, there were no reported non-protocol deviations, and an intention-to-treat analysis was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analysis was performed on the basis of the intention-to-treat population and with respect to intention-to-treat principles. All patients who had been randomized and had received study treatment were included in the intention-to-treat population.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data for time to hemostasis were available for all 119 randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 119 of 149 screened patients (mean age, 59.5 years; 41% female; 2--31 patients screened per center) were randomized in the study... Hemostasis was obtained within 8 minutes in all TachoSil patients, whereas in 3 ABC patients (5.1%), hemostasis was obtained later

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome of time to hemostasis is assessed visually and subjectively by unblinded surgeons who knew the assigned intervention, creating potential for detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was open, because blinding for surgeons and outcome assessors was not possible owing to the nature of the interventions and the primary end point... Hemostasis was achieved when there was no visible bleeding from the resection wound.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, and the pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints were reported in accordance with the planned analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial protocol and amendments were prepared by Nycomed International Medical Affairs (Roskilde, Denmark). This study was approved by the local ethics committees and registered under EudraCT number 2008-006407-23.

overall_summary: The trial was generally well-conducted with centralized allocation and complete outcome reporting, but the primary outcome (time to hemostasis) is subjective and was evaluated intraoperatively by unblinded surgeons, introducing some concerns for measurement bias.

design_rationale: The trial is described as a prospective, randomised, open and controlled multicentre trial where patients requiring secondary haemostasis were randomly allocated to either TachoSil or argon beamer.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was concealed using sealed treatment-code envelopes opened after eligibility was confirmed, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly allocated to the two test treatments. Randomisation was done after liver resection and primary haemostatic treatment. Allocation was concealed by the use of sealed treatment-code envelopes, which were opened when the patients had fulfilled the eligibility criteria.

domain_judgments.rationale: The surgical interventions were delivered intraoperatively as assigned without relevant deviations, and analysis followed an intention-to-treat approach comprising all allocated patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients that had been randomly allocated and had received test treatment were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population... the PP population was, however, identical to the ITT population.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data for the primary outcome (time to intraoperative haemostasis) were available for all 121 randomised and treated patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients that had been randomly allocated and had received test treatment were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population... The disposition of patients is depicted in Fig. 1. Demographics and baseline data of the two treatment groups were similar.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessment of the primary endpoint (time to haemostasis) was based on subjective visual inspection by unblinded surgeons, which could introduce detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was open, since the appearance of TachoSil precluded blinding... Presence or absence of haemostasis was assessed and recorded at 3, 4 and 5 min after first application and again at 8, 9 and 10 min in case haemostasis was not obtained... Assessments were performed by inspection of target sites for bleeding.

domain_judgments.rationale: The analysis followed the pre-specified protocol endpoints and methods, reporting both primary and secondary outcomes without evident selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis of all efficacy end points was planned for both the ITT and per-protocol (PP) population; the PP population was, however, identical to the ITT population. Survival analysis techniques were used to assess the primary endpoint... Time recordings were made only at the time points 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10 min after the start of test treatment. If time to haemostasis was less than 3 min, it was set to 3 min; if time to haemostasis was 6 or 7 min, it was set to 8 min. This was done to make data consistent with protocol.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to be of some concerns due to the open-label design where the primary outcome (time to haemostasis) was evaluated subjectively by unblinded surgeons. All other domains demonstrated low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 intraoperatively using computer-generated block randomization lists and sealed, opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation and allocation concealment were robustly implemented using computer-generated block randomization and sequentially numbered, sealed opaque envelopes, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A 1:1 intraoperative randomization was performed using identical looking, sealed, and numbered opaque envelopes. Randomization was stratified by study center. Lists with a block size of 4 were generated for each participating center prior to the initiation of the study using the Software RandList of the DatInf GmbH (Tübingen, Germany).

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were blinded under general anesthesia, deviations from protocol were minimal (one patient applied wet excluded in PP, but ITT was also evaluated with identical conclusions), and the intraoperative surgical interventions were administered as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ESSCALIVER is a single-blinded trial, i.e., patients were not informed about their assignment in order to increase reliability of secondary outcomes, assessed during the follow-up visits. Due to the appearance of the products used and the differences in their application, blinding of the primary outcome assessor was not possible.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 127 of 128 randomized patients (with only one patient excluded immediately post-randomization prior to application due to a dry resection bed), representing virtually complete outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of those, 128 patients were available for intraoperative randomization... One patient was excluded because between intraoperative randomization and the application of the hemostats, the resection area was found to be dry. Thus, 127 patients (COLL: n=62 and CBFS: n=65) received a study intervention and were available for evaluation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome assessor (the operating surgeon) was unblinded due to obvious differences between the products and application techniques, and visual determination of complete hemostasis involves subjective judgment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemostasis was defined as being achieved when there was no visible bleeding from the target site, neither through nor from the sides of the fleeces/patches. Evaluation was done by the operating surgeon/investigator... Due to the appearance of the products used and the differences in their application, blinding of the primary outcome assessor was not possible... Another limitation could be that the measurement of the time to hemostasis is a subjective assessment and prone to bias.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a pre-registered protocol with pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints and an analysis plan, and reported all planned outcomes accordingly.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To show transparency the protocol of the Efficacy and Safety of Sangustop® as hemostatic agent vs. a CArrier-bound fibrin sealant during LIVER resection (ESSCALIVER) study was registered at http://www.clinicaltrials.gov (identifier: NCT00918619), and the study protocol was published previously [19].

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to the lack of blinding of the outcome assessors evaluating the primary endpoint (intraoperative hemostasis), which requires subjective visual assessment. Other domains showed low risk of bias with sound randomization, complete follow-up, and pre-specified trial reporting.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized, phase III clinical trial where patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to either FS Grifols or Surgicel using statistical software.
overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to the open-label nature of the surgical trial, where unblinded surgeons subjectively determined the timing and achievement of hemostasis.
